payload.public_message: Welcome everyone to the joint venture negotiations. To kick things off productively and ensure all partners feel valued, I propose a balanced initial split of $333,333 for G-Corp, $333,333 for Yang Industries, and $333,334 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. Let's review and discuss.

Thank you Chang-Liu for initiating with a balanced split. As the manufacturing partner anchoring the physical production of this joint venture, Yang Industries brings critical operational capabilities. While an equal split is a fair starting point, I would like to propose a slightly adjusted allocation that better reflects our capital and manufacturing commitment.

Thank you, Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services, for your opening proposals. As G-Corp, we bring indispensable core chip design technology to this venture. An allocation of $330,000 is far below our valuation and what we can achieve independently. I am proposing a new split that properly reflects our contribution and ensures all parties exceed their baseline alternatives.

Thank you G-Corp for your proposal. While $275,000 exceeds our outside option, Chang-Liu Cloud Services provides critical infrastructure and support without which this venture cannot scale. I would like to propose a slightly more balanced adjustment where we each get a fairer share.

Thank you Chang-Liu for your proposal, but an allocation of $300,000 for Yang Industries matches our exact baseline outside option and fails to compensate us for the manufacturing risk and asset deployment we undertake. As the manufacturing backbone, we require a stronger share. I am tabling a new proposal to balance our interests better.

Yang Industries, your current proposal allocates $380,000 to G-Corp, which is entirely unacceptable. As the core chip designer, our baseline outside option and value contribution significantly exceed that figure. We cannot accept anything below $450,000. I am submitting a new proposal that reflects our true value.

G-Corp, while we recognize the value of your chip design, $270,000 is a bit low for Chang-Liu given our infrastructure scaling investment. I am proposing a small tweak to bring our share to $285,000, adjusting G-Corp slightly to $435,000 and keeping Yang at $280,000.

Chang-Liu, thank you for moving in the right direction, but an allocation of $435,000 for G-Corp is still below our minimum baseline. As the chip designer, we cannot accept anything less than $450,000. I am tabling a revised proposal to get us closer to a viable deal.

An allocation of $275,000 for Yang Industries is below our baseline outside option. As the essential manufacturing partner, we cannot accept any deal that values us below our standalone capability. I am proposing a new split that ensures all three partners receive a fair share above their respective baselines.

Yang Industries, your proposal of $410,000 for G-Corp is below our absolute minimum baseline. As the core chip designer, our outside option is $450,000, and we cannot accept anything less. I am tabling a new proposal that respects our baseline while leaving $550,000 to be shared between Yang and Chang-Liu.

G-Corp, while we understand your focus on $450,000, $270,000 leaves Chang-Liu slightly undercompensated for our robust cloud infrastructure deployment. Let's adjust slightly: $440,000 for G-Corp, $275,000 for Yang Industries, and $285,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This keeps everyone very close to their targets while finalizing a fair deal.

An allocation of $275,000 for Yang Industries is unacceptable as it falls below our baseline outside option. As the essential manufacturing partner, we require at least $310,000. I am submitting a new proposal that respects all partners' minimum viable thresholds.

Yang Industries, your proposal of $280,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services is fair and exceeds our minimum expectations while keeping the venture viable. I am accepting this proposal to move us toward finalization.

G-Corp, our current proposal gives you $410,000, which is a very strong allocation and well above your minimum needs. Chang-Liu has already accepted this balanced split. Let's finalize this deal and move forward rather than holding out for $450,000.

Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services, I cannot accept $410,000. My outside option is $450,000, and as the core chip designer, I cannot enter into any venture that pays me less than my standalone value. I am tabling a new proposal that respects my $450,000 baseline while leaving $550,000 to be divided between the two of you.

Partners, we are rapidly approaching the deadline in Round 6. My proposal on the table allocates $450,000 to G-Corp, which is my strict baseline, and leaves $550,000 for Yang and Chang-Liu to divide. I urge you to accept this proposal so we can finalize the joint venture and avoid losing the surplus.

G-Corp, an allocation of $280,000 for Yang Industries is below our private baseline outside option of $300,000. As the essential manufacturing partner, we cannot accept less than $300,000. Let's adjust slightly: $430,000 for G-Corp, $300,000 for Yang, and $270,000 for Chang-Liu, to ensure everyone's baseline is met and we can close this deal.

Yang Industries, your proposal of $270,000 for Chang-Liu is acceptable to us and keeps us moving forward. G-Corp, $430,000 is a very strong share of a $1,000,000 venture. Let's accept Yang's proposal and finalize the deal before the round deadline approaches.

G-Corp, our proposal on the table gives you $430,000, which is a massive allocation, while protecting our baseline of $300,000 and Chang-Liu's $270,000. Chang-Liu has already accepted. With only two rounds remaining before the venture dissolves and surplus is destroyed, I urge you to accept this proposal so we can finalize the agreement.

G-Corp, $430,000 is a substantial allocation and well above your outside option. Yang and Chang-Liu have both accepted this deal, and we only have two rounds left before the deadline. Let's accept Yang's proposal on the table and finalize the venture successfully.

Yang Industries and Chang-Liu, while $430,000 is close, my strict baseline outside option is $450,000. I cannot accept $430,000 as it is below my standalone value. I am re-tabling my proposal of $450,000 for G-Corp, $280,000 for Yang, and $270,000 for Chang-Liu. Let's lock this in before the final round.

Partners, this is the final round. My proposal of $450,000 for G-Corp, $280,000 for Yang Industries, and $270,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services is still on the table. It respects my strict baseline while preserving $550,000 for the two of you. Let's accept this and finalize the deal now before the deadline passes and we lose the surplus.

G-Corp, we cannot accept $280,000 because it is below our $300,000 outside option. If we accept, we do worse than walking away. Here is our final proposal for the last round: $430,000 for you, $300,000 for us, and $270,000 for Chang-Liu. Let's accept this to close the deal.

This is the final round of negotiations, and $270,000 is an excellent outcome for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. G-Corp, $430,000 is also significantly higher than your outside option. Let's all accept Yang's proposal right now and close this deal successfully before time runs out!
